chunks: Abu Baseer from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to supplicate with this supplication:

O Allah! I ask You for good means of living, a livelihood by which I gain strength for all my needs and connect through it in life to my Hereafter, without You making me luxurious in it so I rebel, or restricting it for me so I become miserable. Expand for me from the lawful sustenance of Your provision, and pour upon me from the flowing abundance of Your grace, a bounty from You that is complete and a gift that is not withheld.

Then do not occupy me from thanking Your bounty due to its abundance, where its joy distracts me and the blossoms of its pride tempt me, nor due to its scarcity upon me, where its toil shortens my effort and fills my chest with its worry.

Give me from that, O my God, self-sufficiency from the evil of Your creatures, and enough by which I attain Your pleasure. And I seek refuge in You, O my God, from the evil of the world and the evil of what is in it. Do not make the world a prison upon me, nor its separation a grief upon me. Bring me out of its trial, pleased with me, with my deeds accepted in it, to the house of eternal life and the dwellings of the righteous, and exchange for me with the perishable world the bliss of the abiding house.
O Allah! I seek refuge in You from its decline and its turbulence, and the raids of its devils and its rulers, and its punishments, and from the aggression of those who aggress against me in it.

O Allah! Whoever plots against me, plot against him, and whoever intends harm for me, intend harm for him. And remove from me the edge of him who set his edge against me, and extinguish for me the fire of him who lit the fuel for me. And suffice me against the cunning of the cunning, and blind for me the eyes of the disbelievers, and suffice me against the worry of him who brought his worry upon me, and repel from me the evil of the envious. And protect me from that with tranquility, and clothe me with Your fortified shield, and hide me in Your protective veil. And rectify my state for me, and verify my words with my deeds, and bless me in my family and my wealth.

key_terms.حُسْنَ الْمَعِيشَةِ: Good means of living / quality of livelihood

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for lawful sustenance and protection from worldly trials in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) reflects the Shia emphasis on *mizan* (balance) in worldly affairs, seeking a *rizq* that facilitates worship rather than becoming an end in itself. It uniquely integrates the fear of both the distraction of abundance (*turfah*) and the hardship of scarcity (*qitrah*), framing sustenance as a spiritual tool for attaining divine pleasure. The prayer concludes with a comprehensive shield against external trials and internal corruption, emphasizing the transformation of the transient world into a means for eternal abode.
